svg.title: When the next breath comes before the lung has emptied
svg.desc: Idealized passive linear model with illustrative numbers, not patient data; pressures in cm H2O relative to atmospheric pressure at the airway opening. Panel A plots the volume of a slow unit above its relaxed volume, FRC, in mL per 100 mL entering each breath, against time, with 3 seconds per breath. In the top trace, with enough time, every exhalation returns to the dashed FRC line. In the bottom trace, with 2 seconds to exhale and a 2.5 second time constant, each exhalation is cut short, so end-expiratory volume climbs in shrinking steps of +45, +20, +9, +4 and +2, to 45, 65, 74, 78 and 80 mL, approaching a new plateau of about 82 mL drawn as a dotted line; the trapped volume above FRC is hatched. A note adds that with 5 seconds to exhale the plateau is about 16 mL. Panel B shows the start of one breath with intrinsic PEEP of 10 as three traces on a shared time axis of about 1 second. Alveolar pressure starts at +10 and falls steadily through the dashed airway-opening line at 0 to slightly below 0. Flow starts below the zero line, labeled expiratory flow still present, reaches zero as alveolar pressure reaches 0, and only then becomes inspiratory. Volume falls slightly, is flat as flow crosses zero, then rises once inspiratory flow begins. A hatched band over the first half second marks the threshold: pressure without volume change, effort and energy spent, almost no mechanical work. Under the heading pressure requirement is not work, a solid box gives the simplified, elastic-only pressure requirement at a compliance of 0.05 L/cm H2O: intrinsic PEEP 10 plus 10 for the breath, a peak of 20 cm H2O versus 10. A dashed box, labeled a different quantity, gives work as pressure times volume change: elastic work rises from 2.5 to 7.5 cm H2O·L, 0.25 to 0.74 J, with resistive work not shown. A note for a ventilated patient with a pressure trigger set 2 below airway-opening pressure and no external PEEP gives the effort needed as about 10 plus 2, or 12 cm H2O. A terms strip defines dynamic hyperinflation as volume above FRC, intrinsic PEEP as the recoil pressure from that volume at end-expiration, and external PEEP as pressure set at the airway opening.
